name: Linh Ung Pagoda, Son Tra
kicker: The sea-facing Quan The Am on Son Tra
summary: Ride out along the Son Tra peninsula to Linh Ung Pagoda, where a 67-meter Quan The Am stands on a lotus pedestal at Bai But and looks out to sea. Climb through the gate and up the stair to her feet. The ride and the terrace take half a day, best in clear weather.
timeNeeded: Half a day with the ride
getThere: Bai But, about 10 km northeast of the center, by car or Grab.
heroCaption: The face and the raised hand of the Quan The Am

notice.title: Do not ride the loop in rain
notice.body: The peninsula road is the visit. Do not ride a loop you do not know in the rain.

body: The pagoda is at Bai But, on the Son Tra peninsula, about 10 kilometers northeast of the center. Ride out, then walk the terrace. The Quan The Am stands 67 meters, on a lotus pedestal 35 meters across, facing the sea. The pagoda opened on 30 July 2010.
You walk up through the gate and the stair before you are under the statue. The peninsula road is the rest of the half-day. Do not treat the visit as a short stop between the beach and dinner.

figures.caption: The gate and the stair up to the terrace
figures.alt: The ornate gate and stone stair at Linh Ung Pagoda on the Son Tra peninsula

gettingThere: Linh Ung is at Bai But, on the Son Tra peninsula, about 10 kilometers northeast of the center. Go by car or Grab. It is not a walk from My Khe unless you are already on that shore.

legs.heading: From Da Nang
legs.body: By car or Grab to Bai But, about 10 kilometers northeast of the center.

admissionNote: No entry fee on the city portal or in the 6 June 2017 recognition. Check on arrival if a gate asks for one.
